raw.raw:
The potion goes down bitter and warm. The bleeding stops. The swelling across the bridge of your nose settles.

[ITEM_LOST:Potion of Healing]
[HP:+10]
[CONDITION_REMOVED:Bloodied Nose]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]

The man against the terminus stone is alive. Barely. Chest moving in shallow pulls. Skin the colour of old wax. His clothes are Sandpoint-cut, practical, salt-destroyed. A rope coil at his hip. A knife still sheathed. Whatever happened here, he didn't fight his way out of it.

He didn't need to fight. He just couldn't leave.

His eyes are open. Watching you come down the last steps. No fear in them. No surprise either.

Just relief. The exhausted kind. The kind that comes after hope has mostly gone.

His mouth moves.

"Corven," he says. Barely sound at all. "Is Corven."

He can't finish it. Doesn't need to.

[QUEST_STEP:Aldus Vareth|Reach Aldus Vareth alive|true]
[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[XP:300]
[ARC_COMPLETE:The Glassworks]
[COMPANION_RELATIONSHIP:Daeris|Ammut|Cautious Ally]

Frizwick crouches beside him. Two fingers at his throat. Looks up at you.

"Alive. Not well."

Frizwick grabs Aldus by the collar. Drags him. No ceremony. His heels scrape stone.

You wedge the charge into the crack. Deep as it'll go. The stone here is old and already fractured. Cooperative, almost.

You get behind the terminus stone. Frizwick has Aldus against the far wall, body over his, head down. Good.

You light it.

The fuse burns fast in the damp air. Faster than you'd like.

Then the cave comes apart.

Not a boom. More like the world clearing its throat. A deep crack and a rush of pressure and the wall opens. Salt water floods through. Cold. Immediate. Kneedeep in seconds.

The terminus stone shudders.

The spiral rune on its face brightens. Once. Holds. Then dims.

Something moves in the fluid rushing past your boots. Not water. That blue-white glow. One of the intake channels has ruptured above. The reservoir is leaking through the breach, not the controlled dissolution sequence, just bleeding out into the sea.

Not ideal.

Also not entirely wrong.

[ITEM_LOST:Blasting charge]

Frizwick has Aldus upright. Barely. His weight is mostly hers.

The water is still rising.

She looks at you across the cave.

"We should leave," she says. Conversational. Like she's suggesting it might rain.

The water is at your thighs now. Cold enough to hurt.

You move fast. Around the terminus stone. Along the far wall. Hands on rock, feeling for gaps, for draft, for anything.

The green light is fading as the blue-white bleeds through. Makes it harder.

[DICE:Perception check|18|success]

There. North wall. Low. A shelf of rock and behind it a gap, roughly body-width, the smell coming through it is open air and kelp and something dead. A tidal passage. It goes somewhere. Whether somewhere is up is the question.

You get back to Frizwick. Point.

She looks at it. Looks at Aldus. He's conscious but his legs aren't cooperating fully.

"He goes first," she says. "You push, I pull."

The water hits your waist the moment you get him to the gap. He goes through on his belly, Frizwick hauling from the other side, you with both hands on his boots. The stone scrapes him. He doesn't complain. Good man.

Frizwick next.

Then you.

The passage is thirty feet of black rock and cold water and no dignity whatsoever.

Then it opens.

Sea air. Grey sky. The north face of Thistletop above you, the headland rising sheer. A narrow ledge. Waves breaking ten feet below.

Shalelu's ledge.

[SUBLOCATION:Thistletop - North Face Ledge]
[SKILL_SUCCESS:Perception]

There are no stairs here.

The ledge is forty feet of wet rock. The headland rises above. Sheer face, old handholds cut into it, goblin-made or older, hard to say. The kind of climb that's unpleasant when you're fresh.

Aldus is not fresh. Neither are you.

Frizwick looks up. Looks at Aldus. Looks at you.

"I'll take his weight," she says. "You go first. Find the holds. Call them down."

Reasonable. You start up.

[DICE:Climbing check|15|success]

The handholds are shallow but solid. You call each one down as you find it. Frizwick translates for Aldus. Left foot. High right. Push don't pull. He manages. Barely. She's got a fist in his belt the whole way, taking his weight on the hard moves.

Halfway up he stops. Breathing. Just breathing.

"Keep moving," Frizwick says. Quiet. Not unkind. Matter of fact.

He keeps moving.

You come over the rim onto the headland. Grass and wind and the smell of the sea. You reach back. Take Aldus by the wrist and haul.

He comes over the edge and lies flat on his back and stares at the grey sky.

Frizwick pulls herself up beside him.

"That's everyone," she says.

[SKILL_SUCCESS:Climbing]
[SUBLOCATION_LEAVE]

You kneel beside him. Hands moving. Systematic.

No blade wounds. No breaks you can find. His wrists are raw, rope burn or worse, and there's bruising across his ribs that suggests something squeezed him. Not hard enough to crack. Hard enough to remind him it could.

His eyes are tracking. That's good.

What isn't good is the colour of his skin where the water soaked through. Pale going grey at the extremities. Cold exposure. Hours of it, maybe more. The cave held him and the cave was cold and the cave didn't care.

He needs warmth. Food. Water that isn't salt.

He's watching you work.

"You're not Corven," he says. Clearer now. The fresh air helping.

"No," you say.

He processes that. Closes his eyes briefly.

"He sent you?"

Close enough.

"He's in Sandpoint," you say. "Waiting."

Something moves across Aldus's face. Too complicated to name. Relief and grief and something that might be guilt. The whole weight of whatever happened down there, still on him.

Frizwick has already pulled her spare travel wrap out. Drops it over him without comment.

He's mobile. Slowly. He'll make Sandpoint if you move carefully and don't push the pace.

The rope bridge is gone, of course. You sawed it yourself.
